6	import Mathlib

8	/-!
9	# Field base change is faithful (S10 substrate: the uniqueness half of Galois descent)
10	
11	Milne's descent pattern for the Albanese universal property (III §6.4) is
12	*uniqueness-first*: one proves the factorisation `f = ofCurve P ≫ g` over `k̄`, where
13	the geometry is available, and then descends `g` to `k`.  The classical write-up runs
14	that descent through Galois cohomology — a cocycle for `Gal(k̄/k)`, a spreading-out
15	argument to a finite level, and Galois descent of the resulting morphism.
16	
17	**The uniqueness half needs none of that.**  `∃!` splits into existence and
18	uniqueness, and *uniqueness descends for free along every field extension whatsoever*
19	— not just Galois ones, not just algebraic ones.  The reason is one line:
20	
21	> `Spec L ⟶ Spec k` is flat and surjective for every field extension `k → L`, hence
22	> the base-change functor `Over (Spec k) ⥤ Over (Spec L)` is faithful.
23	
24	Faithfulness is exactly the statement that an equation between two morphisms of
25	`k`-schemes may be checked after base change.  So a `k`-morphism out of the Jacobian
26	is pinned by its `k̄`-avatar, and the *uniqueness* clause of
27	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` over `k` follows from the uniqueness clause over `k̄`
28	with no Galois theory, no cocycles, and no finite-level spreading out.
29	
30	What this file does *not* do is descend **existence**: producing a `k`-morphism from a
31	`k̄`-morphism is where the Galois cocycle genuinely lives, and no part of it is
32	addressed here.  The value of separating the two halves is that it removes the
33	uniqueness clause from the Galois budget entirely, and it does so at arbitrary — in
34	particular *infinite* — extensions, which is precisely the staging that the Wave-6
35	recon (`informal/w6-albanese-port-recon.md` §4.2) recorded as "pinned nowhere":
36	there is nothing to pin, because faithfulness does not care whether `k → k̄` is
37	finite.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.epi_pullback_fst_algebraMap` — the base change of
42	  `Spec L ⟶ Spec k` along any `k`-scheme is an epimorphism (flat + surjective).
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.faithful_baseChange` — **the substrate**: base change along any
44	  field extension `k → L` is a faithful functor `Over (Spec k) ⥤ Over (Spec L)`.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_baseChange_map_eq` — its element form: two `k`-morphisms
46	  agreeing after base change to `L` are equal.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_of_subsingleton_baseChange` — the shape the
48	  descent consumes: a `Hom`-set over `k` is a subsingleton as soon as the
49	  base-changed `Hom`-set over `L` is.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_of_baseChange_subsingleton` — **the uniqueness-first
51	  descent step**: given existence over `k` and uniqueness over `L`, conclude `∃!`
52	  over `k`.
53	
54	The base-change functor is spelled `Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
55	(algebraMap k L)))`, i.e. verbatim `AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L` of
56	`Challenge.lean:170`; this file is stated against the raw spelling so that it does not
57	import the statement file.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false

62	universe u
63	
64	open CategoryTheory Limits
65	
66	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
67	
68	section
69	
70	variable (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
71	
72	/-- The base change of the field extension morphism `Spec L ⟶ Spec k` along an
73	arbitrary `k`-scheme `Z` is an **epimorphism** of schemes.
74	
75	Both hypotheses of `Flat.epi_of_flat_of_surjective` are stable under base change:
76	`Spec L ⟶ Spec k` is flat (a field extension is a flat ring map) and surjective (it
77	hits the unique point of `Spec k`), so its pullback `pr₁` along `Z ⟶ Spec k` is flat
78	and surjective too. -/
79	theorem epi_pullback_fst_algebraMap {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
80	    Epi (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) := by
81	  haveI : Flat (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) :=
82	    MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _ inferInstance
83	  haveI : Surjective (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) :=
84	    MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _ inferInstance
85	  exact Flat.epi_of_flat_of_surjective _
86	
87	/-- **Base change along a field extension is faithful.**
88	
89	For any extension of fields `k → L` — no finiteness, separability, normality or
90	algebraicity assumed — the functor `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L` on `k`-schemes is
91	faithful.  This is mathlib's `Over.faithful_pullback` fed by
92	`epi_pullback_fst_algebraMap`: `Over.pullback f` is faithful as soon as every base
93	change of `f` is epi, and for `f = Spec L ⟶ Spec k` that is flatness plus
94	surjectivity.
95	
96	This single instance is the whole uniqueness half of `k̄ → k` Galois descent: an
97	identity of morphisms of `k`-schemes may be verified over `k̄`. -/
98	instance faithful_baseChange :
99	    (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).Faithful :=
100	  haveI : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)),
101	      Epi (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) :=
102	    fun _ g => epi_pullback_fst_algebraMap k L g
103	  Over.faithful_pullback _
104	
105	variable {k L}
106	
107	/-- **Descent of an equation of morphisms along a field extension**: if two morphisms
108	of `k`-schemes become equal after base change to `L`, they were already equal.  The
109	element form of `faithful_baseChange`. -/
110	theorem eq_of_baseChange_map_eq {X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))} {f g : X ⟶ Y}
111	    (h : (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).map f
112	      = (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).map g) :
113	    f = g :=
114	  (faithful_baseChange k L).map_injective h
115	
116	/-- **Descent of uniqueness**: if the `L`-points `X_L ⟶ Y_L` of the base-changed pair
117	form a subsingleton, so do the `k`-morphisms `X ⟶ Y`.
118	
119	This is the form the Albanese descent consumes.  Note the direction: subsingleton-ness
120	is *pulled back* from the big field to the small one, which is why the geometric
121	uniqueness argument may be run over `k̄` and then read off over `k`. -/
122	theorem subsingleton_of_subsingleton_baseChange {X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))}
123	    (h : Subsingleton
124	      ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).obj X ⟶
125	        (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).obj Y)) :
126	    Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
127	  ⟨fun _ _ => eq_of_baseChange_map_eq (h.elim _ _)⟩
128	
129	/-- **The uniqueness-first descent step, packaged.**
130	
131	Milne 6.4's `∃!` over `k` is assembled from two inputs of quite different cost:
132	
133	* `hex`, *existence over `k`* — the part that genuinely needs the Galois cocycle
134	  (or any other construction of a `k`-rational morphism), supplied by the caller;
135	* `hL`, *uniqueness over `L`* — the geometric argument, run over `k̄` where the
136	  symmetric-power/birationality machinery is available.
137	
138	The conclusion is `∃!` over `k`.  Nothing here is specific to the Albanese setting:
139	`u` is any `k`-morphism and the predicate is factorisation through it. -/
140	theorem existsUnique_of_baseChange_subsingleton {X J A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
141	    (u : X ⟶ J) (f : X ⟶ A)
142	    (hex : ∃ g : J ⟶ A, f = u ≫ g)
143	    (hL : Subsingleton
144	      ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).obj J ⟶
145	        (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).obj A)) :
146	    ∃! g : J ⟶ A, f = u ≫ g := by
147	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hex
148	  exact ⟨g, hg, fun _ _ => (subsingleton_of_subsingleton_baseChange hL).elim _ _⟩
149	
150	end
151	
152	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataAbel
7	
8	/-!
9	# The genus-zero Jacobian is the terminal object, and its universal property is free
10	
11	S11 of the Wave-6 plan: Milne assumes `0 < g` throughout III §§5-6, but the frozen
12	challenge target `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` carries **no genus hypothesis**, so the
13	`g = 0` case has to be discharged separately.  The recon
14	(`informal/w6-albanese-port-recon.md` §3, row S11) sized it as `Jacobian C ≅ 𝟙_` plus
15	Milne I 3.9 (every rational map `ℙ¹ ⇢ A` to an abelian variety is constant), with "zero
16	portable or landed support".
17	
18	**Milne I 3.9 is needed only for existence.**  The `∃!` splits, and the two clauses have
19	very different prices:
20	
21	* *uniqueness* of the factorisation `f = ofCurve P ≫ g` is `cancel_epi`, needing only
22	  that `d.ofCurve P` is an epimorphism.  In the degenerate case that is nearly free:
23	  `d.J` is the base, so `d.ofCurve P` is the structure morphism of a nonempty
24	  `k`-scheme, every morphism to `Spec` of a field is flat, and flat + surjective is epi;
25	* *existence* of some `g` is where the geometry lives — it is exactly the constancy of
26	  `f`, i.e. Milne I 3.9.  This file does not prove it and does not pretend to; it is an
27	  explicit hypothesis of `existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_epi`.
28	
29	So the file's contribution is the reduction, plus a precise account of what is left.
30	
31	## The reduction (this file's actual theorem)
32	
33	`isTerminal_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot`: **if `Pic⁰_{C/k}(T)` is the trivial subgroup for
34	every test `T`, the representing object `d.J` is a terminal object of
35	`Over (Spec k)`.**  This is pure transport of the universal property
36	`homEquiv : (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T` across `Subsingleton`/`Nonempty`, and it is
37	free: no genus, no `ℙ¹`, no rational maps, no Milne I 3.9.
38	
39	Note carefully what the hypothesis is.  It is *not* `genus C = 0`.  Deducing
40	`pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥` from `genus C = 0` is a genuine piece of curve theory — for
41	`T = Spec k` it is the classical "a genus-0 curve with a rational point is `ℙ¹`, whose
42	degree-0 classes are trivial", and for general `T` it is the relative statement.  That
43	implication is **not** proved here and is not claimed; it is isolated as the single
44	mathematical debt of S11, and it is where all the cost of the leaf actually sits.  What
45	this file buys is that the debt is *one implication about Picard groups* rather than the
46	Milne I 3.9 geometry the recon budgeted for.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.subsingleton_hom_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot` — the
51	  `Hom`-set into `d.J` is a subsingleton when the degree-zero group vanishes.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.isTerminal_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot` — **the
53	  reduction**: vanishing `Pic⁰` on all tests makes `d.J` terminal.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.epi_of_epi_left` / `isIso_hom_of_isTerminal` /
55	  `epi_of_isTerminal_of_surjective` — the `Epi (d.ofCurve P)` input, **discharged** from
56	  terminality plus nonemptiness of the curve rather than assumed.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_epi` — the Albanese `∃!`
58	  from `Epi (d.ofCurve P)` plus bare existence.  The existence hypothesis is stated
59	  explicitly rather than hidden.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot` —
61	  **S11 assembled**: vanishing `Pic⁰` plus a nonempty curve give the uniqueness clause
62	  outright, leaving only existence.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCurve_eq_of_isTerminal` — in the terminal case the
64	  Abel–Jacobi map is the unique morphism `C ⟶ d.J`, so it carries no information; this
65	  is the precise sense in which the genus-0 Jacobian is trivial.
66	-/
67	
68	set_option autoImplicit false
69	
70	universe u
71	
72	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
73	
74	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
75	
76	namespace JacobianData
77	
78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
79	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
80	
81	/-- If the degree-zero Picard group of `C` at the test `T` is the trivial subgroup, then
82	`T` has at most one morphism to the representing object.  Transport of `homEquiv` across
83	`Equiv.subsingleton`. -/
84	theorem subsingleton_hom_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
85	    (h : pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥) : Subsingleton (T ⟶ d.J) := by
86	  haveI : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) := by rw [h]; infer_instance
87	  exact Equiv.subsingleton d.homEquiv
88	
89	/-- **The genus-zero reduction.**  If `Pic⁰_{C/k}(T)` is trivial for *every* test object
90	`T`, then the representing object `d.J` is terminal in `Over (Spec k)`.
91	
92	Existence of a morphism `T ⟶ d.J` is `homEquiv.symm 1` (the trivial class always exists,
93	so the `Hom`-set is never empty); uniqueness is
94	`subsingleton_hom_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot`.  Together they are exactly `IsTerminal`.
95	
96	This carries no genus hypothesis: it is the statement that a functor with trivial values
97	is represented by a terminal object.  The curve-theoretic input `genus C = 0 →
98	pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥` is the caller's obligation and is not proved anywhere in this
99	tree. -/
100	noncomputable def isTerminal_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot (d : JacobianData C)
101	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥) : IsTerminal d.J :=
102	  IsTerminal.ofUniqueHom (fun _ => d.homEquiv.symm 1)
103	    (fun T f => (subsingleton_hom_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot d (h T)).elim f _)
104	
105	/-- An `Over`-morphism is an epimorphism as soon as its underlying scheme morphism is:
106	epi-ness in `Over S` is tested on the left components. -/
107	theorem epi_of_epi_left {X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))} (u : X ⟶ Y) (h : Epi u.left) :
108	    Epi u := by
109	  refine ⟨fun {Z} a b hab => ?_⟩
110	  ext
111	  exact (cancel_epi u.left).mp (congrArg Over.Hom.left hab)
112	
113	/-- The structure morphism of a **terminal** object of `Over (Spec k)` is an isomorphism:
114	a terminal object is canonically the base itself (`Over.mkIdTerminal`), and transporting
115	the identity along that iso gives `IsIso J.hom`. -/
116	theorem isIso_hom_of_isTerminal {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} (hJ : IsTerminal J) :
117	    IsIso J.hom := by
118	  have e : J ≅ Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) := hJ.uniqueUpToIso Over.mkIdTerminal
119	  have hwJ : e.hom.left ≫ (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))).hom = J.hom := Over.w e.hom
120	  haveI : IsIso e.hom.left := ((Over.forget _).mapIso e).isIso_hom
121	  haveI : IsIso (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))).hom := by
122	    change IsIso (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))); infer_instance
123	  rw [← hwJ]; infer_instance
124	
125	/-- **Any morphism into a terminal object of `Over (Spec k)` out of a surjective source
126	is an epimorphism.**  This is what discharges the `Epi` hypothesis of
127	`existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_epi` in the degenerate case, with no hand-waving:
128	
129	* `J` terminal makes `J.hom` an isomorphism (`isIso_hom_of_isTerminal`);
130	* the triangle `u.left ≫ J.hom = X.hom` (`Over.w`) then transfers both `Surjective`
131	  and `Flat` from `X.hom` to `u.left`, since both properties cancel on the right
132	  against an isomorphism;
133	* every morphism to `Spec` of a field is flat, so `X.hom` supplies flatness for free
134	  and the only genuine input is surjectivity of `X.hom` — i.e. `X` is nonempty.
135	
136	Flat + surjective is epi (`Flat.epi_of_flat_of_surjective`), and epi on the left
137	component is epi in `Over` (`epi_of_epi_left`). -/
138	theorem epi_of_isTerminal_of_surjective {X J : Over (Spec (.of k))} (hJ : IsTerminal J)
139	    (u : X ⟶ J) (hs : Surjective X.hom) : Epi u := by
140	  haveI : IsIso J.hom := isIso_hom_of_isTerminal hJ
141	  have hw : u.left ≫ J.hom = X.hom := Over.w u
142	  haveI : Surjective u.left := by
143	    rw [← MorphismProperty.cancel_right_of_respectsIso (@Surjective) u.left J.hom, hw]
144	    exact hs
145	  haveI : Flat u.left := by
146	    have hf : Flat X.hom := inferInstance
147	    rw [← MorphismProperty.cancel_right_of_respectsIso (@Flat) u.left J.hom, hw]
148	    exact hf
149	  exact epi_of_epi_left u (Flat.epi_of_flat_of_surjective _)
150	
151	/-- **The Albanese `∃!` when the Abel–Jacobi map is epi.**
152	
153	Uniqueness of the factorisation is `cancel_epi`, and nothing else: the geometric input
154	is entirely inside `Epi (d.ofCurve P)`.  For the genus-zero Jacobian that hypothesis is
155	cheap — `d.J` is then the base `Spec k`, `d.ofCurve P` is the structure morphism of a
156	nonempty `k`-scheme, and every morphism to `Spec` of a field is flat, so
157	`Flat.epi_of_flat_of_surjective` (via `epi_of_surjective_left`) supplies it from
158	surjectivity alone.
159	
160	The existence hypothesis `hex` is *not* removable and is not hidden: a morphism
161	`g : d.J ⟶ A` out of a terminal `d.J` is a point of `A`, and `f` factors through
162	`ofCurve P` exactly when `f` is constant.  Over a genus-0 curve that constancy is what
163	Milne I 3.9 supplies.  What this lemma records is that the *uniqueness* clause — the
164	half the frozen target and the descent lane both need — costs nothing beyond `Epi`. -/
165	theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_epi (d : JacobianData C)
166	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) [Epi (d.ofCurve P)] {A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
167	    (f : C ⟶ A) (hex : ∃ g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g) :
168	    ∃! g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g := by
169	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hex
170	  refine ⟨g, hg, fun g' hg' => ?_⟩
171	  apply (cancel_epi (d.ofCurve P)).mp
172	  rw [← hg, ← hg']
173	
174	/-- **S11 assembled: the Albanese `∃!` for a degenerate Jacobian.**
175	
176	From vanishing `Pic⁰` on all tests plus a nonempty curve, the `uniqueness` clause of
177	the frozen `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` is fully discharged — no genus hypothesis, no
178	`ℙ¹`, no rational maps.  Only existence remains, and it is the explicit `hex`.

10	/-!
11	# S10 at the datum level: the Albanese uniqueness clause descends from `k̄` to `k`
12	
13	`Albanese/BaseFieldFaithful.lean` proves that base change along an arbitrary field
14	extension is a faithful functor on `Over (Spec k)`.  This file spends that on the
15	Wave-6 descent leaf, at the interface the frozen gate actually consumes: the Jacobian
16	datum `d : JacobianData C` and its transport `d.baseChange L`.
17	
18	The point of contact is a definitional one.  `JacobianData.baseChange`
19	(`Picard/JacobianDataBaseChange.lean:60`) is *defined* with representing object
20	
21	```
22	(d.baseChange L).J = (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj d.J
23	```
24	
25	so a morphism out of the base-changed Jacobian **is** a morphism out of the base change
26	of `d.J`, with no comparison isomorphism in between.  Faithfulness therefore applies on
27	the nose, and the uniqueness clause of `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` over `k` follows from
28	the same clause over `L`.
29	
30	## What this buys, and what it does not
31	
32	The recon (`informal/w6-albanese-port-recon.md` §3, row S10) budgeted the whole leaf as
33	"finite-level spreading + Milne-6.4 uniqueness-first Galois argument + the
34	`(Jacobian C)_{k̄} ≅` representing-object comparison", with "nothing" landed or portable.
35	Two of those three items are not needed for uniqueness:
36	
37	* **no finite-level spreading out** — faithfulness holds at `k → k̄` directly, since it
38	  needs only flatness and surjectivity of `Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`, neither of which sees
39	  finiteness.  §4.2's worry that the staging "at the *non-finite* extension k̄ is pinned
40	  nowhere" dissolves: there is nothing to stage;
41	* **no representing-object comparison** — `(d.baseChange L).J` is the base change of
42	  `d.J` by definition, so `uniqueUpToIso` is not in the path at all.  (A comparison
43	  *is* needed if one insists on relating `d.baseChange L` to some independently produced
44	  datum `dL` on `C_L`; `uniqueUpToIso` covers that, and `subsingleton_hom_of_descends`
45	  below is stated so the caller may route through either.)
46	
47	What remains genuinely Galois is **existence**: producing a `k`-morphism `d.J ⟶ A` from
48	a `k̄`-morphism.  Nothing here addresses it.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.subsingleton_hom_baseChange_descends` — uniqueness of
53	  morphisms out of the base-changed Jacobian descends to uniqueness over `k`.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange` — **the S10
55	  uniqueness half**: given the factorisation over `k` and uniqueness over `L`, the
56	  Albanese `∃!` holds over `k`.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.eq_of_baseChange_eq` — the raw descent of an equation
58	  between two morphisms out of the Jacobian.
59	-/
60	
61	set_option autoImplicit false
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	namespace JacobianData
70	
71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	  (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
74	
75	/-- **Descent of an equation between morphisms out of the Jacobian.**  Two `k`-morphisms
76	`d.J ⟶ A` that agree after base change to `L` are equal.
77	
78	The `L`-side equation is literally an equation of morphisms
79	`(d.baseChange L).J ⟶ (baseChange k L).obj A`, because `(d.baseChange L).J` is defined as
80	`(baseChange k L).obj d.J`; no transport is involved. -/
81	theorem eq_of_baseChange_eq (d : JacobianData C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
82	    {g g' : d.J ⟶ A}
83	    (h : (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).map g
84	      = (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).map g') :
85	    g = g' :=
86	  eq_of_baseChange_map_eq (L := L) h
87	
88	/-- **Uniqueness descends.**  If the base-changed Jacobian has at most one morphism to
89	`A_L`, then `d.J` has at most one morphism to `A`.
90	
91	This is the shape Milne's uniqueness-first pattern needs: run the geometric argument
92	over `k̄`, where the symmetric-power and birationality machinery lives, and read the
93	conclusion off over `k`. -/
94	theorem subsingleton_hom_baseChange_descends (d : JacobianData C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
95	    (h : Subsingleton ((d.baseChange L).J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
96	    Subsingleton (d.J ⟶ A) :=
97	  subsingleton_of_subsingleton_baseChange (L := L) h
98	
99	/-- **The S10 uniqueness half of the Albanese universal property.**
100	
101	Assembles the frozen `∃!` over `k` from:
102	
103	* `hex` — existence of *some* factorisation over `k`.  This is the Galois-cocycle half
104	  and is supplied by the caller; it is not proved here;
105	* `hL` — uniqueness of morphisms out of the base-changed Jacobian, i.e. the geometric
106	  argument run over `L = k̄`.
107	
108	No Galois group, no cocycle, no spreading out to a finite level appears in the proof:
109	the descent is `Over.pullback`-faithfulness of a flat surjective base, which is
110	insensitive to whether `k → L` is finite, separable, or algebraic. -/
111	theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange (d : JacobianData C)
112	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : C ⟶ A)
113	    (hex : ∃ g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g)
114	    (hL : Subsingleton ((d.baseChange L).J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
115	    ∃! g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g := by
116	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hex
117	  exact ⟨g, hg, fun _ _ => (subsingleton_hom_baseChange_descends L d hL).elim _ _⟩
118	
119	/-! ## The general case: uniqueness proved for an *independently produced* datum over `L`
120	
121	The lemmas above take the `L`-side uniqueness at `(d.baseChange L).J`, the transport of
122	`d`.  But the way the geometry is actually available is different: over `k̄` one produces
123	a datum `dL : JacobianData C_L` in its own right (that is where the symmetric-power and
124	birationality machinery lives), and there is no reason for `dL` to be `d.baseChange L` on
125	the nose.
126	
127	This is exactly the place where a representing-object comparison *is* needed — so the
128	claim "S10 needs no comparison" must be read narrowly: it holds for the transported
129	datum, not for an arbitrary one.  The comparison is cheap, though, and it is already
130	landed: `JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` is an isomorphism of representing objects, and
131	transporting a `Subsingleton` of a `Hom`-set along an isomorphism of its source costs
132	two rewrites.  So the general case is not a new mathematical obligation, only one more
133	step. -/
134	
135	/-- `Subsingleton` of a `Hom`-set transports along an isomorphism of the source. -/
136	theorem subsingleton_hom_of_iso {D : Type*} [Category D] {X X' Y : D} (e : X ≅ X')
137	    (h : Subsingleton (X' ⟶ Y)) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
138	  ⟨fun f g => by
139	    have hh : e.inv ≫ f = e.inv ≫ g := h.elim _ _
140	    have := congrArg (fun t => e.hom ≫ t) hh
141	    simpa using this⟩
142	
143	/-- **The S10 uniqueness half, for uniqueness proved at an arbitrary `L`-datum.**
144	
145	`dL : JacobianData C_L` is any datum on the base-changed curve — in particular one
146	produced over `k̄` by the geometry, with no relation to `d` assumed.  Uniqueness at
147	`dL.J` transports to `(d.baseChange L).J` through `uniqueUpToIso` (both represent
148	`Pic⁰_{C_L/L}`, so they are canonically isomorphic), and thence down to `k` by
149	faithfulness.
150	
151	Together with `existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange` this covers both stagings, and
152	records honestly that the comparison is unavoidable in this one — cheap, but present. -/
153	theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange_datum (d : JacobianData C)
154	    (dL : JacobianData ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C))
155	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : C ⟶ A)
156	    (hex : ∃ g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g)
157	    (hL : Subsingleton (dL.J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
158	    ∃! g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g :=
159	  existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange L d P f hex
160	    (subsingleton_hom_of_iso ((d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL) hL)
161	
162	end JacobianData
163	
164	end AlgebraicGeometry

neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :

/--
The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
-/

    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)

functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
